documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology clinic. Seen 01/30/2025.

58-year-old woman with dermatomyositis and osteoporosis, referred for spells of spinning brought on by head position: tilting her head up, turning in bed. She has no hearing loss, ringing or sense of fullness in either ear.
BP 135/85. HR 78, regular.
Neurological examination normal apart from the Dix-Hallpike test, which brought on her vertigo with nystagmus that settled within 60 seconds. No carotid bruit. No JVD. No cardiac murmur.

Impression: benign paroxysmal positional vertigo.
Canalith repositioning (Epley) performed in clinic and tolerated. Taught home repositioning exercises. No imaging needed. Follow up as needed if spells persist after several weeks of exercises.

reports.text: Liquid-based cervical cytology, specimen adequate, transformation zone present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV not detected.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual visit.
Since last year: dermatomyositis diagnosed by rheum in August, treated with prednisone and methotrexate. Finished the last prednisone at the start of this month per their taper; stays on MTX 15 weekly + folic acid. Strength nearly back, rash gone. Neurology in January called the spinning spells BPPV and did a repositioning maneuver; she's had maybe one brief spell since and does the exercises. Swallowing about the same, manageable. Hip same.
Psych: stable, sees psychiatry every 3 months, same meds.
No falls. PHQ-9 2.
Meds: HCTZ 25, haloperidol 5, benztropine 1, raloxifene 60, D3 1000, methotrexate 15 mg weekly, folic acid 1, acetaminophen prn. Prednisone off.
Exam: BP at goal. Eyelids and knuckles without rash. Heart regular, lungs clear. Proximal strength 5-/5. No edema. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal; Pap/HPV collected.
A/P
- Dermatomyositis, improving: per rheumatology. CBC and CMP today double as MTX monitoring; will fax to rheum.
- Osteoporosis: two years on raloxifene plus a 7-month steroid course. Repeat DXA ordered.
- BPPV: improved.
- HTN controlled. Esophageal dysmotility, severe R hip OA: stable.
- Schizophrenia: psychiatry; metabolic labs today.
- HCM: mammogram 12/24 negative; Pap/HPV today; colonoscopy 2019.

documents.title: Labs and Pap
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CBC, CMP (liver tests normal on MTX), lipids, A1c all normal. Pap negative, HPV negative. Results to patient; CBC/CMP faxed to rheumatology.

reports.study: DXA bone density, hip and spine
reports.text: Comparison: 01/24/2023, same scanner. Lumbar spine L1-L4: T-score -2.5. Left femoral neck: T-score -0.9. Left total hip: T-score -0.7. No significant change from prior at any site.
reports.conclusion: Osteoporosis at the lumbar spine, stable. Hip density normal, stable.

documents.title: Bone density
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your bone scan is unchanged from two years ago, which is a good result, especially with the prednisone in between. Keep the raloxifene and vitamin D going.

documents.title: Refills
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Refill requests for HCTZ 25 mg and raloxifene 60 mg, 90 days each, approved per protocol. Raloxifene PA renewal resubmitted to MassHealth with the 3/25 DXA; approved.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up - HTN
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
BP check, routine.
Taking HCTZ daily. No headaches, no lightheadedness. Rheum saw her in spring, dermatomyositis quiet on methotrexate. Vertigo hasn't come back. Psych unchanged.
She brought a flyer about a research study of a new blood pressure pill and asked whether she should sign up. We went over what a trial like that involves: she'd be assigned by chance to the new drug or a placebo, neither she nor the study doctors would know which, and the study would probably ask her to stop or adjust her HCTZ, with extra visits and BP checks. Her BP is well controlled on a cheap, familiar drug, which matters in weighing it. She's free to call the study team with questions; no decision needed from me. She took the flyer home to think it over.
Meds unchanged: HCTZ 25, haloperidol 5, benztropine 1, raloxifene 60, D3, methotrexate 15 weekly, folic acid, acetaminophen prn.
Exam: BP and HR as charted, at goal. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.
A/P: HTN controlled, continue. CBC/CMP today (MTX monitoring too, copy to rheum). Annual visit due March. Flu/COVID in the fall.

documents.title: Labs from yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood counts, kidney and liver tests are all normal. Copy faxed to rheumatology. No changes.

documents.title: Refills
documents.author: MA
documents.body: HCTZ 25 and raloxifene 60, 90-day refills sent. Reminded pt by phone that her annual visit is due in March; she'll call to book. She says she had her flu shot at the pharmacy.

documents.title: Emergency department note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Outside emergency department, 01/28/2026. Abbreviated record.
59F, schizophrenia stable on haloperidol and benztropine, here with three weeks of her head pulling to one side and episodes of her eyes rolling up. Painless but upsetting and getting in the way of her day.
Meds per pt: haloperidol, benztropine, HCTZ, raloxifene, methotrexate weekly, folic acid, acetaminophen. NKDA.
Exam: sustained neck muscle contraction tilting the head to one side, chin turned toward the opposite shoulder. No fever, no signs of infection or injury.
CBC, CMP, TSH: within normal limits.
Impression: oculogyric crisis / acute dystonia due to antipsychotic.
Treatment: diphenhydramine 50 mg IV with improvement.
Disposition: discharged home with her partner. Contact psychiatrist within the next few days to review haloperidol. Follow up with PCP.

documents.title: ER visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I went to the emergency room last week because my neck kept twisting and my eyes were going up. They gave me something in the IV and it calmed down. They said it's from the haloperidol. I have a call in to my psychiatrist.

documents.title: Re: ER visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry you went through that, Bernice. I'm glad it settled. Yes, please keep after your psychiatrist this week, since the medicine question is theirs to sort out. If it comes back, go back to the ED. I'd like to see you too; the front desk will reach out to set up a visit.

documents.title: Scheduling attempt
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called pt to book PCP follow-up after ED visit. No answer, voicemail left with callback number. Portal message sent as well.

documents.title: Annual visit reminder
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Bernice, our records show you're due for your annual wellness visit. Please call or reply here to pick a time.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Refill requests for HCTZ 25 and raloxifene 60. Not seen since 8/2025; PCP approved 90 days each with a note that she needs a visit before further refills. Message left for pt.

documents.title: Emergency department and admission note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Outside hospital, ED and neuro ICU. Date of arrival: 07/25/2026. Abbreviated record sent at PCP request.
Brought in by ambulance after collapsing at home. Partner states she complained of the worst headache of her life moments before she lost consciousness. On arrival somnolent, rousable to voice.
History: schizophrenia, hypertension, dermatomyositis, osteoporosis, esophageal dysmotility, BPPV, oculogyric crisis on antipsychotic in January.
Home meds: HCTZ 25 mg, haloperidol 5 mg, benztropine 1 mg, acetaminophen 500 mg prn (per partner; list incomplete).
NKDA.
BP 160/95, HR 55.
Neuro: right pupil dilated and unreactive to light, right upper lid ptosis.
CT head without contrast: hyperdense blood in the basal cisterns, consistent with subarachnoid hemorrhage.
CT angiography head: aneurysm of the right posterior communicating artery.
Assessment: subarachnoid hemorrhage from ruptured right posterior communicating artery aneurysm.
Plan: neurosurgery consulted; admitted to the neuro ICU for securing of the aneurysm and monitoring.

documents.title: Call from partner
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt's partner called (listed contact, verbal HIPAA authorization on file). Bernice collapsed at home Saturday night with a sudden severe headache; taken to the hospital and found to have bleeding around the brain from a ruptured aneurysm. Partner says the neurosurgeons sealed the aneurysm with coils on Sunday and she is still in the neuro ICU. Wanted us to know. Asked the hospital's HIM department by fax for her records. PCP notified.

documents.title: PCP note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Informed by partner of SAH from a ruptured R PComm aneurysm, coiled, in neuro ICU at an outside hospital. Records requested. Will reach out to the family once she is closer to discharge.
